messages.subject: Fitting Random Effects to Different Groups
parts:
Hi,

I have data where there are diseased and non-diseased individuals from different geographic areas. I would like to fit a model that contains random effects for area for each disease group (diseased and healthy). I have done this in INLA by creating two additional area vectors, the diseased one has NAs for non-diseased individuals and the healthy on has NAs for the diseased individuals. I then include both of these in my model using f(area_diseasegroup, model="iid"). Is this the correct way to include these random effects? I have found that by fitting these models, the random effects for area in each of the disease groups are simply the negatives of the other...

Thanks,
Michelle

Hi

I think your setup is correct, like if

ii = c(1:n, rep(NA,n))
jj = c(rep(NA,n), 1:n)

then

~ ..... + f(ii, model="iid") + f(jj, model="iid")

would add a iid term to each group with a group spesific precision.


if you get 'strange' results, then we need to look into the model itself
as its coded, and then we need to rerun it here; just send it to
he...@r-inla.org
